hints: Focus on the number of lone pairs on the central atom, as lone pair repulsion squeezes bond angles smaller.
Compare $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ with two lone pairs (about $104.5^\circ$) to $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ with one lone pair (about $107^\circ$).
Check each pair in turn and ask if the first angle is really smaller than every angle in the second species.
walkthrough:
**Recall the VSEPR rule**

Think of electron pairs pushing each other apart. The repulsion order is lone pair-lone pair > lone pair-bond pair > bond pair-bond pair.

So more lone pairs means a smaller bond angle: $$\text{tetrahedral } 109.5^\circ > \text{pyramidal } \sim107^\circ > \text{bent } \sim104.5^\circ$$

**Work out the shapes and angles**

Count bonding pairs and lone pairs on the central atom for each species.

$\text{CH}_4$: 4 bond, 0 lone, tetrahedral, $109.5^\circ$. $\text{SF}_6$: 6 bond, 0 lone, octahedral, $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$.

$\text{CO}_2$: 2 bond, 0 lone, linear, $180^\circ$. $\text{BF}_3$: 3 bond, 0 lone, trigonal planar, $120^\circ$.

$\text{H}_2\text{O}$: 2 bond, 2 lone, bent, $104.5^\circ$. $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$: 3 bond, 1 lone, trigonal pyramidal, $\sim107^\circ$.

$\text{NH}_4^+$: 4 bond, 0 lone, tetrahedral, $109.5^\circ$. $\text{NH}_3$: 3 bond, 1 lone, pyramidal, $107^\circ$.

**Compare first with smallest of second**

For A, $109.5^\circ$ is larger than $90^\circ$. For B, $180^\circ$ is larger than $120^\circ$. For D, $109.5^\circ$ is larger than $107^\circ$.

Only for $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$, $104.5^\circ$ is smaller than $107^\circ$, because two lone pairs squeeze more than one.

options.A: $\text{CH}_4$ is tetrahedral with $109.5^\circ$. $\text{SF}_6$ is octahedral with smallest angle $90^\circ$. The first angle is larger, not smaller, so this pair fails the test.
options.B: $\text{CO}_2$ is linear with $180^\circ$. $\text{BF}_3$ is trigonal planar with $120^\circ$. The first angle is much larger than the second, so this is the opposite of what is asked.
options.C: $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ has 2 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs, bent shape, $104.5^\circ$. $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ has 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair, pyramidal shape, about $107^\circ$. Two lone pairs repel more strongly, so the first angle is smaller than the second.
options.D: $\text{NH}_4^+$ has no lone pairs, tetrahedral, $109.5^\circ$. $\text{NH}_3$ has one lone pair, pyramidal, $107^\circ$. The first angle is larger because removing the lone pair opens the angle up, so this pair is the wrong way round.
